entries.target: wine:Brennan’s Essential by Piper-Heidsieck Extra Brut NV
entries.value: Brennan's Essential is our house Champagne, an Extra Brut from Piper-Heidsieck, labelled for us. Its bubbles come from a second fermentation in the bottle, and it's very dry: citrus, orchard fruit, brioche and a firm, chalky finish. That dryness and fine bubbles cut rich, salty food, so it's our first pick with the Grand Isle Jewel Oysters, the Eggs Hussarde and the Turtle Soup, and the second choice with the Louisiana Oysters, the Creole Caesar and the Crab & Corn Omelette. We pour it at 43 to 46°F in a tulip, easing the cork out with a quiet sigh. Piper-Heidsieck was founded in Reims in 1785.

entries.target: wine:Pierre Sparr Brut Rosé Crémant d’Alsace NV
entries.value: The Pierre Sparr is a Crémant d'Alsace rosé, which must be all Pinot Noir. It's made like Champagne, with the second fermentation in the bottle and at least 18 months on its lees: dry, with strawberry, red currant and a creamy mousse. Red fruit for raw beef and bubbles for the crisp shell make it our first pick with the Steak Tartare Cannoli, and the second choice with the Steak Tartare with Rye, the Poussin à la Moutarde, the Eggs Sardou and the Eggs Owen. We pour it at 43 to 46°F in a flute, in two stages. Sparr dates its family roots to 1680.

entries.value: Rare Brut is a prestige vintage Champagne, first made in 1976 at Piper-Heidsieck, declared only in exceptional years, and its own house since 2018. It's Chardonnay-led with Pinot Noir from grand and premier cru villages, a single harvest left long on its lees: golden, with white peach, candied citrus, toasted almond and a long, fine mousse. It's the step up from our house Champagne for a celebration, glorious with raw oysters and crab, or as a toast on its own. We pour it by the glass at 46 to 50°F in a tulip, from a bottle kept fresh under a Coravin Sparkling stopper.

entries.value: The Argyle Brut is American sparkling wine from Oregon's Willamette Valley, the 2022: recent vintages blend Chardonnay and Pinot Noir with a little Meunier, made the Champagne way, with the second fermentation in the bottle. Brut means dry, and this one shows shortbread and apple, citrus zest and a saline finish. Dry bubbles cut through salt and fat, so it shines with oysters and anything fried. We pour it by the glass at 43 to 46°F in a flute, in two stages so the mousse doesn't overflow. Argyle opened in 1987 in Dundee, in a former hazelnut plant, with sparkling wine its signature from the first year.

entries.value: Pazo das Bruxas is Albariño from Rías Baixas, on the Atlantic coast of Galicia in Spain, made by Familia Torres; the name means manor of the witches. It's unoaked and bottled young: lemon, white peach and a saline, almost sea-spray snap. That salty freshness makes it our first pick with the Gulf Fish en Papillote and the Creole Caesar, the still white with the Grand Isle Jewel Oysters, and the second choice with the Swordfish Grenobloise, the Fish Bouillabaisse and the Tuna Crudo. We pour it at 45 to 48°F in a white wine glass and keep it iced, because the freshness fades as it warms.

entries.value: Famille Durand's Val de Loire Sauvignon Blanc comes from the Loire Valley, where vineyards follow the river for hundreds of miles, a cool region of crisp, fresh wines. It's bone dry and zippy, grapefruit and cut grass with a flinty note. Artichokes flatten many wines or make them taste oddly sweet, but this sharp, herbal acidity stands up to them and meets the tarragon in the Choron, so it's our first pick with the Eggs Sardou, and the second choice with the Creole Tomato Tostada and the Louisiana Crab Claws. We pour it at 45 to 48°F in a white wine glass, from the ice bucket.

It shows white flowers and citrus, a chalky texture and gentle richness. Rich enough for butter and fresh enough for seafood, it's our first pick with the Redfish Véronique, the Louisiana Crab Claws in their brown butter vinaigrette and the Crab & Corn Omelette, and the second choice with the Turtle Soup. We pour it by Coravin, a needle through the cork, into a white Burgundy bowl at 50 to 54°F, and I'll show you the label first.

entries.value: Fichet's Château London is a Mâcon-Igé: Chardonnay from Domaine Fichet, a family estate founded at Igé, in Burgundy's Mâconnais, in 1976. Château London is a named slope of old limestone, not a castle; the name traces to an owner on the rue Landon in Paris. Made mostly in steel with a touch of old oak, it's apple and citrus, gently round with a fresh finish. On our Dinner Tasting Menu that roundness meets the butter on the Louisiana BBQ Lobster, and the freshness cuts the ’nduja. We pour 4 oz at 50 to 53°F in a white wine glass, from a cooler, never an ice bath.
entries.reason: Five-star review of the description: it named the founders, Francis and Christiane Fichet, with nothing in the research showing either has died, and hedged the name's origin (said to come from); it now names the family estate and its founding year only and states the origin as the record does, every other fact kept
